unit.why: A short anecdote: R. Leizer of Hovitch asks his master, R. Yeshaya, how to keep his mind on his tefillin. Following the master's instruction he gains that level, then loses it after telling others about it on Simhat Torah.

stories.start_quote: הה"ק ר׳ ליזר בהגה"ק ר״י חריף
stories.summary_en: A disciple asks his rebbe how never to let his mind stray from his tefillin. The rebbe has him recite Barukh She-amar three times and he attains the level, but he loses it on the day he tells his acquaintances about it on Simhat Torah.

tags.why: Constant awareness of the tefillin is the subject of the story

quotes: הוא הי׳ תלמיד הקדוש ר״ר וישא
tags.why: The disciple asks his master and obeys his instruction
The remedy is reciting the Barukh She-amar prayer
The loss of the level happens on Simhat Torah

quotes: סיפר הרב ז״ל למיודעיו את הענין
tags.why: Telling the episode is itself the turning point of the story

quotes: ומאז והלאה לא הסיח עוד דעתו מהתפילין
tags.why: He reaches a lasting state of attachment, unbroken awareness
He loses his spiritual level after revealing it
Implied lesson that spiritual attainments should be kept hidden

quotes: ומאז והלאה לא הסיח עוד דעתו מהתפילין
tags.why: The rebbe's instruction has a wondrous effect

missing_concepts: loss of a spiritual level (madregah) through revealing it
